newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cyprus stocks fall in becalmed market.
newsitem.headline: Cyprus stocks fall in becalmed market.

text.p: Cyprus's stocks fell in directionless trading on Wednesday, with brokers complaining investors were shunning the market.
The 41-share Cyprus Stock Exchange (CSE) index set at 100 points closed at 80.68 , declining 1.86 percent from its close of 82.21 on Friday.
The market fell 1.28 percent on Monday alone, to 81.16 with declines registered mainly in the banking, insurance and commercial companies' sub indices.
Brokers said the lull on the market reflected general business sentiment at the moment.
"There are a number of investors taking cash out of the market," said Stavros Agrotis of CISCO, the Cyprus Investment and Securities Corporation.
"There is no particular reason. The market is lacking direction and reflecting the economic conditions -- there is a general business stagnation, people are not seeking loans," he said.
The banking sub index closed at 89.27 points, down 1.77 points on Friday's figure of 91.04.
Fully paid shares in the Bank of Cyprus closed at 334.5, down five cents from Friday's close of 339.5. Fully paid shares of the Cyprus Popular Bank shed 8.5 cents to close at 321.5.

The Hellenic Bank closed at 260.5, down 6.5 cents from Friday. Shares in the Universal Savings Bank were the only ones in the sector which did not decline, closing at 135.5 from Friday's closing figure of 135.
The insurance sector sub index closed at 58.57 from 59.08 on Friday. Shares in Universal Life shed 3.5 cents to close at 378.5. Paneuropean Insurance fully paid closed up one cent at 130.
Interamerican Insurance fully paid closed at 99.5, down two cents. Philiki Insurance fully paid shed 9.5 cents and closed at 233.5.

Cement producer Vassiliko closed at 149.5 from its close of 154.5 on Friday. Keo, the Cypriot beer and wine producer, closed at 105.5 from 108 on Friday and half a cent away from its year low of 105 recorded on November 1.
National carrier Cyprus Airways was trading at 39.4 cents from 39.9 cents on Friday. On Tuesday it fell to a year low of 39 cents.
